Urgent against planned is split by page, not by category: the library's emergency column (Emergency plumber and heating engineer, Burst and leaking pipes, Leak detection and repair, Boiler repairs, Central heating repairs, Blocked drains and sinks) switches the emergency variant on when the client confirms call outs; every other page gets the plain briefs. Inside the planned pages the pack's split is carried in the card briefs: schedule led (what slips and when, with the reason in the system) for boiler servicing, central heating servicing, gas safety certificates, oil boilers and the cylinder's yearly check; problem led (symptom, cause in the water or the system, consequence) for radiators, power flushing, taps and basins, toilets, cold water tanks and heating controls where the complaint is rooms too hot or too cold; desire led (the library's desire_led column: the customer's situation, never an invented symptom) for boiler installation, central heating installation, air source and ground source heat pumps, underfloor heating, shower installation when it is a new shower, bathroom installation, gas appliance installation, outside taps and garden plumbing and water softeners. steps.title: Tell Us What's Wrong
steps.brief: How to get in touch and what is useful to say first: what is happening and in which room, whether the heating or the hot water is off, the make of the boiler and the fault code on its display if it shows one, and photos of the boiler, the radiator or the leak if they have them. Nothing behind the boiler's casing is ever a job for the reader. No promise of a reply time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.title: We Look at the System and Price the Job
steps.brief: The visit and what gets looked at: the boiler and its controls, the pipework and the radiators, the water pressure, where the flue and the condensate pipe run, what the system water looks like, how a new boiler or cylinder would get in. Follows [CV: quote_method]; only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it). Gas work is done by an engineer on the Gas Safe Register as a fact of the trade, never a boast; the business's own registration only from [CV: verified_logos] and the accreditation client values.

steps.title: We Fit or Fix It on a Date That Suits You
steps.brief: The date is agreed in advance, to suit the customer. Where a job means a spell without heating or hot water (a boiler or cylinder change, from the trade facts timing cells) say so plainly and leave the length of it to the visit. Never mention the price, the quote or changes to the plan (step 2 and Why choose us own them). Never restates the start time (FAQ 4 owns it).

step_2_no_visit.title: We Price Your Job

Describe how the price is reached only from [CV: quote_method]; when quote_method is blank, name no method at all (no photos, call, video or visit). Only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it).

steps_emergency.title: Call Us
steps_emergency.brief: What to say: what is happening, where the water is, whether the heating or hot water is off, the fault code if the boiler shows one. What to do meanwhile, in plain words: for a leak, the stopcock shut (the trade facts: the internal stop tap turned clockwise) and people kept away from wet electrics; for a smell of gas or a carbon monoxide alarm sounding, the gas emergency line first, before this business, with the number only as the trade facts give it; for a boiler, the fault code and the pressure gauge read and nothing inside the casing touched. The number from [CV: phone]. No promise of a reply or an arrival time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps_emergency.title: We Tell You What We Can Do and When
steps_emergency.brief: An arrival time only as the business gives it on the call: no window or response time written here unless [CV: response_time] is set. A call out charge only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee]; the price for making it safe agreed before anyone comes out only from the price_agreed_before_work practice and [CV: quote_method]; what the repair costs waits until the fault has been seen. Never restates 'free'. 'Same day' only when [CV: same_day_available] is yes; evenings and weekends only when [CV: out_of_hours_available] is yes.

steps_emergency.title: We Make It Safe and Fix What We Can
steps_emergency.brief: What usually happens on the visit, from the trade facts emergency row: the hazard found, the water or the gas isolated, the area made safe, the fault diagnosed, the repair done on the visit where the part is to hand; otherwise the system left safe and a return booked with the part. A gas fitting found unsafe is turned off or disconnected with the customer's permission and not used until it is put right (the trade facts unsafe situations rows). Never promise a same visit fix. Never mention the price.

Say plainly that the heating and hot water are off while the change is made. Nothing about when the job can start (FAQ 4 owns it).

faq_slots.question: Why are some of my radiators cold when the heating is on?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words, each with its part: air trapped at the top of a radiator; sludge settled along the bottom, the deposit a system leaves as it corrodes inside; one radiator cold all over while the rest are hot, which is a valve stuck or the flow never balanced between them. Then what the local water or housing adds, then what is done about each. Never 'needs a new boiler'.

faq_slots.question: Should I repair my boiler or replace it?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Most faults are one part, and a repair is not a replacement. Say honestly what tips it: parts no longer made, a heat exchanger gone, the same fault back more than once in a winter. Never an age as the reason (the trade facts record no verified lifespan) and never a rule that old boilers are banned (the trade facts: no in force ban on replacing a gas boiler in an existing home). Link the boiler repairs or boiler installation page where LINKABLE PAGES has one.

faq_slots.question: Does my boiler really need servicing every year?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rows only: no yearly legal duty for an owner occupier was established; a maker's guarantee usually asks for a yearly service and a record of it; a landlord has a separate yearly gas safety check and record. Say what a service covers (the trade facts boiler servicing stages: the burner, the flue, the safety devices, the maker's own tests) and that it is more than a safety check. No fear selling on carbon monoxide, nothing about the reader's boiler being unsafe. No dates.

faq_slots.question: Who does the gas work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The legal position as a fact of the trade, from the trade facts rows: paid gas work in a home is done by an engineer on the Gas Safe Register, registered for that kind of work, and the customer can check the card and the register. The business's own registration and number only from [CV: verified_logos] and the accreditation client values; when none is on file, the rule alone and nothing about this business. Never a boast, never 'approved' or 'certified' (the register registers).

faq_slots.question: Does a new boiler or heat pump need any permission or paperwork?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Point at the trade facts rule rows (Table C) and write what usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases": a new boiler is notified to building control, which an installer on the right competent person scheme does for the customer; an unvented cylinder the same; an air source heat pump in a garden is usually allowed without a planning application when it meets the conditions on size, position and noise, and a listed home or a flat is different; a ground source heat pump has its own environmental permissions. What the customer does about it only as the row gives it. No figure, no volume, no decibel, never a regulation's, an order's or a scheme's number.

cards.title: Radiators that never get properly hot
cards.brief: Problem led, the pack's Central Heating Service brief: a radiator cold across the top, one cold along its bottom edge, one cold all over while the rest are hot, a room that never warms. The one cause this card makes: water not getting round every radiator. Separate the three in plain words with the part named: air trapped at the top; the deposit a system leaves as it corrodes inside, settled along the bottom; a valve stuck or the flow never balanced between the radiators (the trade facts radiators and power flushing rows). What is done about each, from the stages: bled, cleaned or flushed and treated, the valve freed or changed and the system balanced; the cleaning method chosen for the system, never a machine flush as compulsory (the trade facts). By category: Central Heating Service reads it as the system, its circulation and its water; Gas Engineer as what a service or a flush finds (the water condition and the filter, from the servicing stages); Plumber as a valve weeping or a joint at the radiator letting water out. Never a product, never 'needs a new boiler'.
cards.mechanism: water not getting round every radiator

cards.title: A boiler that keeps cutting out or needing topping up
cards.brief: Problem led: a fault code on the display, a lockout on a cold morning, the pressure gauge down again a week after it was topped up, water under the boiler (the trade facts boiler repairs signs row). The one cause this card makes: water leaving a sealed system somewhere. Name where it usually goes, in plain words: a radiator valve weeping onto the floor, a joint leaking beneath a floor, or the relief valve passing water out through its overflow pipe outside because the expansion vessel has lost its charge of air. Topping the pressure up each week only puts off the find. What a visit does: the fault recorded, the system made safe, the diagnosis made against the maker's instructions, the part changed and the boiler tested (the trade facts stages). By category: Gas Engineer reads it inside the boiler, which is registered gas work and never a job for the reader beyond reading the code and the gauge; Central Heating Service on the system side, the valves and joints, linking the leak detection page where LINKABLE PAGES has one; Plumber as the leak itself. Not a frozen condensate pipe: the seasonal card owns that.
cards.mechanism: water leaving a sealed system somewhere

cards.title: A service or gas check that has slipped
cards.brief: Schedule led, the pack's Gas Engineer brief for planned pages: what slips when a service or a check is missed, written as what the visit catches and never as fear. The one cause this card makes: wear nobody has looked at since the last service. Gas Engineer reads it as the yearly boiler service (the trade facts stages: the installation and its history checked, the boiler and the flue inspected, the maker's own cleaning and tests, the safety devices, the record), what a missed service leaves to wear on through another winter (the skipped row: faults in the flue or the burner found by nobody, deterioration carrying on), and the landlord's yearly check and record: who needs it and when, the record given to the tenants, the early check window as the trade facts rule row gives it, with 'usually' and never the regulation's name; a service is more than a safety check (the trade facts: the maker's inspection and tests on top). For an owner occupier the yearly service is a maker's guarantee condition where the trade facts guarantee row has it, never a legal duty. Central Heating Service reads it as the system check: the water condition, the inhibitor, the filter, the controls (the central heating servicing stages). Plumber reads it as the unvented cylinder's check only as the maker's instructions give it (the trade facts: no universal yearly interval), else the stopcock, the tank in the loft and the overflow looked at. Never fear selling on carbon monoxide, never that the reader's boiler is unsafe.
cards.mechanism: wear nobody has looked at since the last service

cards.title: Water where it shouldn't be
cards.brief: Problem led, the pack's Plumber brief: a tap that drips, a toilet that keeps running or refills on its own, a mark on a ceiling, damp under a basin (the trade facts taps, toilets and leak detection signs rows). The one cause this card makes: a seal, a washer or a joint that has given up. Name the part: the washer or cartridge in the tap, the fill valve or flush valve in the cistern, the seal under the basin waste, a joint on a pipe above the ceiling. Say that the water travels along a pipe or a joist before it comes through, so the mark is seldom under the fault, and that the source is traced before anything is opened up (the trade facts leak detection stages: supply or heating circuit established, the section isolated, the source located, exposed only where it has to be). By category: Plumber reads it across the house; Gas Engineer as water under the boiler or at the condensate pipe; Central Heating Service as a radiator valve or a joint on the heating circuit and the pressure loss that goes with it. Not a burst pipe running now: the emergency variant owns that.
cards.mechanism: a seal, a washer or a joint that has given up

faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing cells: most of this work runs all year; a boiler, cylinder or heating change means a spell without heating or hot water, which is easier to live with in a warm month; a frost is when exposed pipes and condensate pipes freeze, so protection goes in when a frozen pipe is repaired. Nothing about winter being busy or booking ahead. No dates, no promise about the weather.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked: the cause in the water or the system, with the part named and where it is; what the local water hardness or housing era adds, as the research gives it; where the symptom is urgent (water running, a smell of gas), the first safe step before anything else, the gas emergency line first for gas; then what the business does about it. Never that homes in the area have sludge, scale or lead; never anything inside a gas fitting as a job for the reader. One figure at most, and it must come out of a trade facts row.

problem_card.title: The first cold snap finds the weak spot
problem_card.brief: Say first what is normal when the heating goes back on after months off: a radiator or two that needs bleeding, a smell of warm dust, a boiler that takes a cycle to settle. Then what is not: a boiler that locks out on a frosty morning because the condensate pipe where it runs outside has frozen (the pack's seasonal line), a pipe in the loft or an outside tap split after a freeze (the trade facts burst pipes and outside taps rows: freezing is the winter cause), a pump or a valve that seized while it stood. The one cause this card makes: months standing idle, then a hard frost. What a visit does: the pipe thawed and the boiler reset, the burst section replaced with protection against the next freeze (the trade facts stages), the part changed. By category: Gas Engineer reads it in the boiler and its condensate; Plumber in the pipes, the tank in the loft and the outside tap; Central Heating Service in the pump, the valves and the radiators. Nothing about winter being busy or booking ahead, no dates.
problem_card.mechanism: months standing idle, then a hard frost

faq_slot.question: Can [WORK_LOWER] work be done in winter?
faq_slot.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing cells: yes, this work runs all year; a boiler or heating change in winter means a spell without heating while it is done, said plainly; a frost is when exposed pipes and condensate pipes freeze, so a burst found in a cold snap is repaired with protection against it happening again. Nothing about winter being busy. No dates.

cards.title: A burst pipe, or water pouring through a ceiling
cards.brief: Write the reader's situation, why it can't wait and what they do first, in that order: water spraying from a pipe, dripping through a ceiling, running down from a light fitting, a pressure drop with a wet patch spreading (the trade facts burst pipes signs row). The one cause this card makes: water running with nothing to stop it. First, from the trade facts: the stopcock shut (the internal stop tap turned clockwise), people kept away from wet electrics and that circuit left off, then the call. Why it can't wait: the water keeps going into floors and ceilings and towards the wiring while nothing stops it (the skipped row). What usually happens when they call: the supply isolated and the pipe drained, the split section cut out and replaced or repaired, the system refilled and tested, the finishes made good separately; where a freeze caused it, insulation or protection against the next one (the trade facts stages). By category: Plumber leads; Central Heating Service reads it as a heating pipe or a radiator valve letting go; Gas Engineer as water pouring from under the boiler. Never an arrival time, out of hours cover or a call out promise unless [CV: response_time], [CV: out_of_hours_available] or [CV: emergency_callouts] confirms it.
cards.mechanism: water running with nothing to stop it

cards.title: No heating or hot water in the cold
cards.brief: The reader's situation: a fault code on the display, a boiler that will not fire, the pressure gauge at nothing, radiators stone cold in a frost (the trade facts boiler repairs signs row). The one cause this card makes: one fault locking the whole boiler out. What the customer can safely do first: read the fault code and the pressure gauge and tell us what they say; nothing inside the casing, which is registered gas work. Why it can't wait: a cold house, and water standing in pipes that can freeze while the heating is off. What usually happens: the fault diagnosed against the maker's instructions, the part changed where it is to hand, the boiler tested and put back into service; where the part has to be ordered, the system left safe and a return booked (the trade facts stages and the parts availability line). Most faults are one part: never 'needs a new boiler'. A gas fitting found unsafe is turned off with the customer's permission and not used until it is put right (the trade facts unsafe situations rows), written calmly. By category: Gas Engineer leads; Central Heating Service reads it as the pump, a motorised valve or the controls (the central heating repairs stages); Plumber as the hot water cylinder or its immersion heater. Never a same day promise unless [CV: same_day_available] is yes.
cards.mechanism: one fault locking the whole boiler out

cards.title: A smell of gas, or a carbon monoxide alarm sounding
cards.brief: The first call is never this business, and the card says so plainly: the gas emergency line first, with the number only as the trade facts CO row gives it (never one from memory), the fitting turned off, windows opened, and medical advice for anyone with the signs the row lists (headache, dizziness, feeling sick, breathlessness). The one cause this card makes: gas or fumes getting out where they should not. Once the supply has been made safe, finding and fixing the cause is registered gas work (the trade facts rules rows): a connection that leaks, a flue or a vent that lets combustion fumes into the room (the gas appliance installation done badly row). Never fear selling, never 'silent killer', never that the reader's boiler is dangerous because it is old, never 'call us first'. By category: Gas Engineer leads; Plumber and Central Heating Service send the reader the same way and say what this business does after the gas emergency service has been. A CO alarm only as the trade facts rows have it: fitted when a new boiler or heater goes in, and provided by a landlord in a rented room that has one, with 'usually' and never the regulation's name.
cards.mechanism: gas or fumes getting out where they should not

cards.title: The only toilet blocked, or a sink that won't go down
cards.brief: The reader's situation: the only toilet in the house blocked, waste water coming back up a sink or a shower tray, a gurgle from the plughole, a smell from the drain outside (the trade facts blocked drains signs row). The one cause this card makes: a blockage sending waste water back the way it came. Why it can't wait: the waste backs up into the fixtures and can overflow (the skipped row). What usually happens: the fixtures affected identified, the trap or the inspection point checked, the obstruction cleared, the flow tested, and a blockage that keeps coming back investigated for a damaged drain (the trade facts stages). Whose drain it is, from the trade facts: the homeowner's own drain against the sewer company's shared and public sections, with 'usually' and never the Act's name; no water or a flood on the whole street is the water company, said so the reader calls the right people. By category: Plumber leads; Gas Engineer and Central Heating Service read it as the condensate pipe blocked or frozen, which locks the boiler out. Never a chemical the client values do not give.
cards.mechanism: a blockage sending waste water back the way it came

cost.h2: What Moves the Price of an Emergency Call Out in [CITY]

cards.title: The time and the day you call
cards.brief: The time of day and the day of the week move the price: a weekday afternoon against a late night or a Sunday (Table F: out of hours attendance). Say that plainly and give no figure. A call out charge or an out of hours rate only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee] and [CV: price_list]; never say there is no charge for coming out unless [CV: quote_call_out_fee] says there is none. Whether the business comes out at those hours only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]; when it is blank the card says what the hour does to the price and nothing about which hours are covered. The trade facts record no standard call out charge, so never a typical one.

cards.title: How far we come and how we reach the fault
cards.brief: How far the address is from the base and how easy the job is to reach move the price: a house on a main road with room outside against a flat above a shop, a locked gate, a boiler or a tank in a loft, nowhere to park the van. Say why each adds time and give no figure. Never an arrival time unless [CV: response_time] is set, and then only as given; never hours of cover unless [CV: out_of_hours_available] says so. How far the business travels only from [CV: travel_distance].

cards.title: Stopping the water and making it safe
cards.brief: What is done first on this call out and what that takes, from the trade facts emergency, burst pipes and leak rows: the immediate hazard identified, the water isolated (the customer shuts the internal stop tap first where they can), the area and any wet electrics made safe, then the fault diagnosed. A smell of gas goes to the gas emergency line first and is never part of this price. What moves the price: a short exposed section or a fitting that can be isolated against active damage, a split that cannot be reached or a fault that takes finding (the trade facts emergency, burst pipes and leak price rows). Gas work only within the engineer's registration. No figure.

cards.title: What's on the van, and what has to be ordered
cards.brief: What is usually on the van against what has to be ordered (the trade facts emergency, burst pipes and leak price rows): an accessible stocked part fitted on the visit against a specialist part or one that is unavailable on the day. What follows as a second visit, priced as its own job: the system left safe and a return with the part, and the walls, ceilings or floors put back after a burst, which is separate from the pipe repair (the trade facts burst pipes row). A temporary isolation is not a permanent repair, so say which one the customer has. Never promise a same visit fix. Said as what usually happens, never as what this business keeps in stock unless [CV: materials_methods] says so. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

steps.title: Call Us
steps.brief: What to say: what is happening, where the water is, whether the heating or hot water is off, the fault code if the boiler shows one. What to do meanwhile, in plain words: for a leak, the stopcock shut (the trade facts: the internal stop tap turned clockwise) and people kept away from wet electrics; for a smell of gas or a carbon monoxide alarm sounding, the gas emergency line first, before this business, with the number only as the trade facts give it; for a boiler, the fault code and the pressure gauge read and nothing inside the casing touched. The number from [CV: phone]. No promise of a reply or an arrival time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.title: We Make It Safe and Find the Fault
steps.brief: The water or the gas isolated, the area made safe, then the fault diagnosed rather than guessed at (the trade facts emergency and boiler repairs stages: diagnose against the maker's instructions; the leak's circuit established before anything is opened). The customer told what was found. A call out charge only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee]; the price agreed before any work starts only from the price_agreed_before_work practice and [CV: quote_method]. Never restates 'free'.

steps.title: We Fix It, or Leave It Safe and Come Back
steps.brief: The repair done on the visit where the part is to hand; otherwise the system left safe and a date agreed for the return with the part (the trade facts: a feasible repair or a return arranged). A gas fitting found unsafe stays off, with the customer's permission, until it is put right. Never promise a same visit fix; 'same day' only when [CV: same_day_available] is yes. Never mention the price.

faq_slots.question: How much is an emergency [TRADE_PERSON] call out in [CITY]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what moves the price: the time of day and the day, how far the address is from the base, how easy the fault is to reach, and the parts on the day. A call out charge or an out of hours rate only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee] and [CV: price_list]; never say there is no charge for coming out unless [CV: quote_call_out_fee] says there is none. Hours only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]; an arrival time only from [CV: response_time]. How the price is reached only from [CV: quote_method]: making it safe and finding the fault come first, and the repair is priced once the fault has been seen. The price agreed before work starts only from the price_agreed_before_work practice. The trade facts record no standard call out charge, so never a typical one. No figure beyond what those client values hold.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for emergency work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for, with a plausible plumbing example that does not suggest carelessness. Never what it pays or who it covers. Whether the customer's own home policy pays for finding a hidden leak only as their policy says (the trade facts: trace and access cover is never assumed).

faq_slots.question: What happens if the fault comes back after an emergency repair?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then that making it safe is making it safe: the permanent repair is what the work is held to, under the reasonable care and skill standard, never as a defence (the trade facts: a temporary isolation is not a permanent repair). No promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: Is this an emergency, or can it wait?
faq_slots.answer_brief: What counts as urgent, from the card list: water running that the stopcock has not stopped, no heating or hot water in a frost, a smell of gas or a carbon monoxide alarm (the gas emergency line first), the only toilet blocked. What usually waits for a planned visit: a dripping tap, a radiator cold at the bottom, a basin slow to empty, a boiler service, a toilet that refills on its own (the trade facts signs rows). Link one service page. Planned work is never dressed up as urgent.

faq_slots.question: What should I do before you arrive?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rows only: the stopcock shut for a leak and wet electrics left alone; the fault code and the pressure gauge read for a boiler, and nothing inside the casing; for gas, the gas emergency line first, the fitting off, the windows open; a photo of the leak or the display helps. Never an instruction to open a boiler, touch gas pipework or work on an unvented cylinder. Whether the business deals with the home insurer only from the client values.

faq_slots.question: How quickly can you get to me?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: response_time] and [CV: start_time] only, as given; a same day visit only when [CV: same_day_available] is yes; evenings and weekends only when [CV: out_of_hours_available] is yes. Never '24/7', 'round the clock' or 'any time' unless [CV: emergency_callouts] gives it in those words. The trade facts record no standard attendance time, so never a typical one.

faq_slots.question: Do you come out at night and at weekends?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Only from [CV: out_of_hours_available] and [CV: emergency_callouts], in their words; when neither is set, say what happens on a call (the fault talked through, the first safe step, the earliest visit agreed) and nothing about hours. Never '24/7' or 'round the clock' unless the client value gives it in those words.

items.brief: The first stage from the trade facts: the survey, the diagnosis, the check of the supply, the pressure and what is there now. A part of the job, not a promise about the quote.

items.title: Isolating the water or the gas safely
items.brief: The isolation stage from the trade facts: the supply or the circuit shut off and drained where the job needs it, electrics protected. Gas isolation is registered gas work; name only what the rows give.

A named product or make only from [CV: materials_methods].

items.title: The main fit or repair
items.brief: The central stage of the job from the trade facts: the fit, the connection, the part changed, the pipe run, named as the trade names it and in the words a customer uses.

cards.title: The first signs
cards.brief: The things a homeowner notices first, from the trade facts signs row for this service, in their words and with the part named where the row gives it. The one cause this card makes: a fault that has been building for a while. Then what it leads to if left, from the skipped row: specific, never alarming, never a word about carbon monoxide unless the row has it and then only as the fact. On a schedule led page (boiler servicing, central heating servicing, gas safety certificates, oil boilers, the cylinder's yearly check) the card is what slips and when, with the reason in the system and never in the customer's diary: a year of firing wearing the burner seals and the flue joints so the breakdown comes in the first cold week, the inhibitor losing its strength so the water starts to corrode the radiators, the landlord's record running out (the trade facts stages and rule rows; the re dose interval only as the trade facts guidance row has it, never as law).

cards.title: It keeps happening
cards.brief: A radiator bled every week, pressure topped up every month, a sink that blocks again a fortnight after it was cleared, a tap that drips again after a new washer, a toilet that still runs. The one cause this card makes: the symptom treated and the cause left in. Say what the job does to get at the cause, from the trade facts stages and the done badly row for this service: the diagnosis made against the maker's instructions rather than by swapping parts; the circuit a leak is on established before anything is opened; a blockage that comes back traced past the trap to the drain; the valve or the cartridge changed rather than the washer. Never a dig at whoever came before. On a schedule led page: the thing a service or check would have found before it became a call out.
cards.mechanism: the symptom treated and the cause left in

cards.title: It's past patching up
cards.brief: The same fault back more than once in a winter, a part that is no longer made, a heat exchanger gone, a cylinder weeping from its body, a tank in the loft gone soft, pipework so corroded a joint will not take a repair (the trade facts done badly rows and the pack's craft rule: a repair is not a replacement). The one cause this card makes: parts or pipework a repair no longer holds. Say honestly what tips a repair into a replacement and what doing it properly involves, from the stages for the replacement page, and link that page where LINKABLE PAGES has one. Never an age as the reason (the trade facts record no verified boiler lifespan), never every fault as a reason for a new boiler, never a rule that old boilers are banned.
cards.mechanism: parts or pipework a repair no longer holds

cards.title: Hot water and heating that aren't what they were
cards.brief: A shower that runs cooler or weaker than it did, hot water that runs out sooner, radiators slow to warm, a boiler that bangs or rumbles as it heats (the trade facts signs rows for cylinders, showers, power flushing and servicing). The one cause this card makes: scale and sludge building up inside over the years. Name where: scale from hard water on the heat exchanger and in the cylinder and shower; the deposit a corroding system leaves in the radiators and the filter. What the local water adds, as the research gives it (the water company's hardness), never that homes here have scaled up boilers. What the job does: the system cleaned or flushed by the method that suits it and treated, the filter cleared, a softener where the services list has one (the trade facts stages; never a machine flush as compulsory). Not water failing to get round, not a leak: the category page owns those.
cards.mechanism: scale and sludge building up inside over the years

cost.h2: What Affects the Cost of [SERVICE] in [CITY]

cards.title: Like for like, or a change
cards.brief: From the trade facts price row for this service: a same type, same position replacement with its connections reused against a change of type or position (a vented cylinder to an unvented one, a radiator moved, a toilet relocated, a combi in place of a tank and cylinder). Say it plainly and give no figure.

cards.title: Where it is and how we get to it
cards.brief: A concealed cistern, a boiler in a loft, pipes under a solid floor, a leak behind tiles, and the making good after walls or floors are opened, from the trade facts price row. Say why an awkward position costs more time.

cards.title: What the system needs besides the part
cards.brief: The water condition and cleaning, the controls a new boiler needs, a new electrical circuit for a shower or a heat pump, a flue or condensate reroute, the building control route, from the trade facts price row. Say the business looks before it prices, from [CV: quote_method] only. A named product only from [CV: materials_methods].

cards.title: Parts and the number of visits
cards.brief: Maker specific parts, a part no longer stocked, a return visit when it has to be ordered, a fault that takes finding, from the trade facts price row. A call out or diagnostic fee only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee]. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

faq_slots.question: How much does [SERVICE_LOWER] cost in [CITY]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Prices only from [CV: price_list]; otherwise how the quote is given, from [CV: quote_method] only, and a call out fee only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee]. The four cost cards above already give what moves the price: name one factor at most, never the list again.

faq_slots.question: How long does [SERVICE_LOWER] take?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing row only: the trade facts give no standard duration for this work, so give what decides it (a like for like swap against a change, access, whether the system needs cleaning first, a part to order) and no number; the spell without heating or hot water where the row gives one; a screed's drying time only as the underfloor heating row gives it. Nothing about when the job can start unless [CV: start_time] is set. This is the one place the timing is written.

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your [SERVICE_LOWER] work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Start with yes, then the terms from [CV: guarantee_years] and [CV: guarantee_scope]. A maker's guarantee is the maker's, with its conditions (the yearly service, the records, the registration) described from the trade facts guarantee rows, never promised.

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for [SERVICE_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What happens if the fault comes back after the work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: Does [SERVICE_LOWER] need anything signed off or notified?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rule rows for this service only, put as the thing that usually applies, with "usually" or "in most cases". Gas work is done by someone on the Gas Safe Register. A new boiler, an unvented cylinder or a new electrical circuit is notified to building control, which an installer on the right scheme does for the customer; the water company is told for some fittings; a heat pump has its planning conditions and permissions; a landlord's record goes to the tenants. What the customer does only as the row says. Never a regulation's name or number, an Act's name or legal advice. Where the rows give no rule, say no permission is usually needed for this work at a home and leave it there. The business's own registrations only from [CV: verified_logos] and the accreditation client values.

faq_slots.question: What does your [SERVICE_LOWER] service include?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The What's Included items said as a sentence, in other words, naming the work. What it does not cover only from the services list, with one sibling service page or the category page linked.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked: the cause in the water or the system, with the part named and where it is; what the local water hardness or housing era adds, as the research gives it; where the symptom is urgent, the first safe step before anything else, the gas emergency line first for gas; then what this service does about it. Never that homes in the area have sludge, scale or lead; never anything inside a gas fitting as a job for the reader. One figure at most, and it must come out of a trade facts row.

problem_card.title: What the first frost does to it
problem_card.brief: What shows in the first cold spell, from the trade facts signs row for this service. Say first what is normal when the heating comes back on after the summer (a radiator that needs bleeding, a boiler taking a cycle to settle) and then what is not: a pipe in the loft or an outside tap split after a freeze (the burst pipes and outside taps rows: freezing is the winter cause), a boiler locked out on a frosty morning by a frozen condensate pipe (the pack's seasonal line), a drain outside frozen. The one cause this card makes: water freezing where a pipe or a drain runs exposed. Say what the job does about it, from the stages: the burst section replaced and the pipe insulated or protected, the condensate pipe thawed and the boiler reset. Not a fault that has been building (card 1), not scale (card 4).
problem_card.mechanism: water freezing where a pipe or a drain runs exposed

faq_slot.question: Can [SERVICE_LOWER] be done in winter, and how long does it take?
faq_slot.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing row only: this work runs all year; the spell without heating or hot water where the row gives one, said plainly; a frost is when exposed pipes and condensate pipes freeze, so a repair in a cold snap includes protection against the next one; then what decides how long it takes, with no number unless the row gives one. Nothing about winter being busy. No dates. This is the one place the timing is written.

cards.title: An old boiler you're deciding whether to keep
cards.brief: The customer's situation: a boiler that has had a repair or two, a house bought with a boiler nobody knows, an extension to heat, a gas fire or cooker to add. What decides it: what the boiler sits on and whether its parts are still made: the pipework and the system water a new boiler would inherit (the trade facts boiler installation stages: the system cleaned and treated before the new one goes on), the heating demand and the hot water demand that choose a combi or a system boiler (the trade facts: no bedroom count rule), the flue and condensate route, and the faults the old one has been having (parts no longer made, a heat exchanger gone, the same fault back more than once). What the work gives them: the right type of boiler for the house on a clean system, set up and recorded, notified to building control, with the controls the trade facts rule row asks for on a combi in an existing home ('usually', never the standard's name). Leads on the Boiler installation page; Gas appliance installation reads it as the fire, cooker or LPG boiler and the supply, ventilation and flue it needs (the trade facts stages). Never an age as the reason, never a ban or a deadline (the trade facts: no in force ban), never 'hydrogen ready' as more than a maker's description.
cards.mechanism: what the boiler sits on, and whether its parts are still made

cards.title: A house, an extension or a room the heating never reached
cards.brief: The customer's situation: a house with no central heating or with storage heaters, an extension or a loft room, a conservatory, one room that is always cold. What decides it: the heat each room loses and what can deliver it: a room by room heat loss calculation, the radiators or the floor that can give that heat at the flow temperature the heat source runs at, the pipe routes, the floor build up and the covering on top for underfloor heating (the trade facts central heating installation and underfloor heating stages and the covering row: tiles conduct, thick carpet holds the heat back). What the work gives them: a system designed for the house, filled, cleaned, treated and balanced so every room reaches its temperature (the trade facts stages); a warm floor laid on insulation so the heat goes up and not down (the skipped row). Leads on the Central heating installation and Underfloor heating pages. Never a running cost or a saving; the screed's drying time only as the trade facts row gives it, never written here.
cards.mechanism: the heat each room loses and what can deliver it

cards.title: Thinking about a heat pump
cards.brief: The customer's situation: off the gas grid with an oil tank, a boiler near the end of its useful life, an extension, a wish to come off gas. What decides it: whether the house, its radiators and its hot water suit lower temperature heating: a heat loss survey, the radiators assessed at the lower water temperature rather than all replaced (the trade facts radiator sizing row), a cylinder for the hot water, where the outdoor unit can stand and the noise conditions it has to meet, or the ground for a loop or a borehole (the trade facts air source and ground source stages, the planning rows with 'usually' and never the volume, the distance or the decibel figure). What the work gives them: a design for their house and a certified installation; the grant only as the trade facts rows give it, the installer applying and the owner confirming, never a figure or eligibility written here. Leads on the Air source heat pumps and Ground source heat pumps pages. Never a bill saving (the trade facts: a performance figure does not establish a household's running cost), never 'heat pumps don't work in old houses' or its opposite as a promise.
cards.mechanism: whether the house, its radiators and its hot water suit lower temperature heating

cards.title: A bathroom, shower, softener or garden tap you've been meaning to sort
cards.brief: The customer's situation: a new bathroom, a proper shower in place of a trickle over the bath, hard water furring up every kettle and shower head, a tap in the garden for the hose. What decides it: the supply, the waste and the wiring the new fitting needs: the pressure and the hot water supply that choose a mixer or an electric shower and whether a new electrical circuit is needed (the trade facts shower stages and the electrical rule row, with 'usually'), where the waste can run and how the wet area is waterproofed (bathroom installation stages), a drinking tap left unsoftened (the trade facts water softener rows), the route for an outside tap and the protection it needs against backflow and frost (the outside taps stages and rule row: an ordinary hose tap usually needs no water company notice, and does need its check valve). What the work gives them: a fitting that suits the supply the house has, tested and left dry. Leads on the Bathroom installation, Shower installation and repair (a new shower; a shower that has failed is written from the trade facts signs row instead), Water softeners and Outside taps and garden plumbing pages. Never an invented leak or a weak shower as the opener on a new bathroom.
cards.mechanism: the supply, the waste and the wiring the new fitting needs

problem_card.title: Getting it done before the cold or the summer
problem_card.brief: The customer's situation: they want the new boiler in before the cold, the bathroom done before the family comes, the outside tap in for the garden, the heat pump running by autumn. What decides it: the spell without heating or hot water the job needs, from the trade facts timing cells (a boiler, heating or heat pump change interrupts the heating while it is done; a cylinder change interrupts the hot water; a wet screed has to dry at its own pace and is never forced with the heating; an outside pipe wants its frost protection before winter). What the work gives them: a date that suits the house, with the interruption said plainly in advance. No dates, nothing about winter being busy or booking ahead, no promise about the weather.
problem_card.mechanism: the spell without heating or hot water the job needs

Nothing about winter being busy, nothing about when the job can start unless [CV: start_time] is set. This is the one place the timing is written.

cards.title: Where the fault is
cards.brief: A leak you can see at a fitting with a valve to isolate it, or a boiler fault that is quickly identified, against a concealed leak with several possible sources or a fault that takes real diagnosis (Table F leak detection, boiler repairs). Say it plainly and give no figure.

cards.title: Getting to it
cards.brief: An exposed short length of pipe or a boiler with room round it against a split under a floor or behind tiles, a frozen section, or an appliance that is hard to reach (Table F burst and leaking pipes, boiler repairs). Say the business looks before it prices, from [CV: quote_method] only.

cards.title: The part and the testing it needs
cards.brief: How much pipe has to be replaced, a compatible part against a specialist one, and a flue or gas supply defect that means testing again before the job is finished (Table F). A named make only from [CV: materials_methods].

cards.title: Making good after
cards.brief: A wall or a floor opened to reach the fault and put back afterwards, water damage that has already spread, an electrical area the water has reached (Table F: reinstatement, making good). Anything found once it is opened is agreed first only from the extra_work_agreed_first practice. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

cards.title: Water you can't stop
cards.brief: Water spraying from a pipe, dripping through a ceiling, running down from a light fitting, a wet patch spreading while they watch (the trade facts burst pipes signs row). The one cause this card makes: a split or a failed joint on a live supply. Write the reader's situation, what they do first from the trade facts (the stopcock shut, the internal stop tap turned clockwise; wet electrics left alone and that circuit off), why it can't wait (the water keeps going into the floors and ceilings and towards the wiring) and what usually happens when they call: isolated and drained, the damaged section found, cut out and replaced or repaired, refilled and tested, the finishes made good separately; where a freeze caused it, the pipe insulated or protected (the trade facts stages). Leads on the Burst and leaking pipes page. On Leak detection and repair the card is a leak running now whose source is not obvious: the water travels along a pipe or a joist before it shows, so the stain is seldom under the fault; the circuit established, the section isolated, the source located, opened only where it has to be (the trade facts stages). Never an arrival time or a call out promise unless [CV: response_time] or [CV: emergency_callouts] confirms it.
cards.mechanism: a split or a failed joint on a live supply

cards.title: A boiler that's stopped in a cold spell
cards.brief: A fault code, a lockout, the pressure gauge at nothing, radiators cold in a frost, no hot water (the trade facts boiler repairs signs row). The one cause this card makes: a frozen condensate pipe or a single failed part. What the customer safely does first: read the fault code and the gauge and tell us; nothing inside the casing, which is registered gas work. What usually happens: a frozen condensate pipe thawed and the boiler reset (the pack's seasonal line); otherwise the fault diagnosed against the maker's instructions, the part changed where it is to hand, the boiler tested; a part to order means the system left safe and a return booked (the trade facts stages and the parts availability line). A gas fitting found unsafe is turned off with the customer's permission and not used until put right (the trade facts unsafe situations rows), said calmly. Leads on the Boiler repairs page; Central heating repairs reads it as one circuit cold, a pump or a motorised valve, a joint leaking on the heating side (the trade facts stages). On the Emergency plumber and heating engineer page the card also carries the smell of gas and the carbon monoxide alarm: the gas emergency line first, with the number only as the trade facts CO row gives it, the fitting off, the windows open; this business comes after. Most faults are one part: never 'needs a new boiler', never a same day promise unless [CV: same_day_available] is yes.
cards.mechanism: a frozen condensate pipe or a single failed part

cards.title: A smell of gas, or an alarm going off
cards.brief: The first call is never this business, and the card says so: the gas emergency line first, with the number only as the trade facts CO row gives it, the fitting turned off, the windows opened, and medical advice for anyone with the signs the row lists. The one cause this card makes: a gas escape or a flue fault, which the gas emergency line handles first. What this business does afterwards is registered gas work: the connection or the flue found and put right, the fitting tested before it goes back on (the trade facts gas appliance stages and the done badly row: a leaking connection, a flue or vent letting fumes into the room). Leads on the Emergency plumber and heating engineer page; on Boiler repairs and Central heating repairs it is the short card that sends the reader the right way; on the plumbing pages (Burst pipes, Leak detection, Blocked drains) it reads instead as the water company's side: no water or a flood on the whole street is theirs, and whose drain is whose from the trade facts drain ownership row, with 'usually'. Never fear selling, never 'silent killer', never that the reader's boiler is dangerous because of its age.
cards.mechanism: a gas escape or a flue fault, which the gas emergency line handles first

cards.title: Waste water that comes back after you've cleared it
cards.brief: The only toilet blocked, a sink or a shower tray filling with grey water, a gurgle from another plughole when one is emptied, a smell from the drain outside (the trade facts blocked drains signs row). The one cause this card makes: a blockage further down than the trap, so clearing the trap or plunging the bowl brings it back (the done badly row). Why it can't wait: the waste backs up into the fixtures and can overflow (the skipped row). What usually happens: the fixtures affected identified, the trap and then the inspection point checked, the obstruction cleared, the flow tested, a blockage that keeps returning investigated for a damaged drain (the trade facts stages). Whose drain it is, from the trade facts drain ownership row, with 'usually' and never the Act's name. Leads on the Blocked drains and sinks page; on Boiler repairs and the heating pages it reads as a condensate pipe blocked or frozen. Never a chemical the client values do not give.
cards.mechanism: a blockage further down than the trap

cost.h2: What Moves the Price of an Emergency Call Out in [CITY]

cards.title: The time and the day you call
cards.brief: The time of day and the day of the week move the price: a weekday afternoon against a late night or a Sunday (Table F: out of hours attendance). Say that plainly and give no figure. A call out charge or an out of hours rate only from [CV: quote_call_out_fee] and [CV: price_list]; never say there is no charge for coming out unless [CV: quote_call_out_fee] says there is none. Whether the business comes out at those hours only from [CV: out_of_hours_available]; when it is blank the card says what the hour does to the price and nothing about which hours are covered. The trade facts record no standard call out charge, so never a typical one.

cards.title: How far we come and how we reach the fault
cards.brief: How far the address is from the base and how easy the job is to reach move the price: a house on a main road with room outside against a flat above a shop, a locked gate, a boiler or a tank in a loft, nowhere to park the van. Say why each adds time and give no figure. Never an arrival time unless [CV: response_time] is set, and then only as given; never hours of cover unless [CV: out_of_hours_available] says so. How far the business travels only from [CV: travel_distance].

cards.title: Stopping the water and making it safe
